messages:
Anya (crypto): Heads-up: I started drafting a key-rotation strategy for DEKs/KEKs across AWS/GCP/Azure. Need input on automatic rotation vs manual rewrap, backward compatibility for old ciphertext, and rollout timing.

Jess S.: +1 see the draft? link: https://our-internal/wiki/rotation-draft (private)

Anya (crypto): Paste of the important bits below: we currently embed metadata in ciphertext like:
```json
{"v":1, "kms":"aws", "key":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/old", "enc":"<base64>"}
```
Plan A: automatic KEK rotate in KMS (rotate-key) and rely on KMS to unwrap old DEKs when needed. Pros: low lift. Cons: depends on provider semantics and audit linkage.

Mike (eng-ops): Question: when you say "automatic", do you mean scheduled key rotation (KMS-native) or our service rotating the wrapped DEKs and updating stored ciphertext?

Anya (crypto): Good call. Two options:
- KMS-native rotation (AWS/GCP) = create new key version; KMS will unwrap previous DEK versions as long as key material is available. We don't rewrap DEKs.
- Service-driven rewrap = generate new DEK, re-encrypt plaintext or rewrap existing DEK with new KEK and write new ciphertext blob in DB.

Lisa SRE: Rewrap at scale worries me: re-encrypting millions of rows will spike IOPS and KMS API quotas. We need throttling, background job, and fallback if workers crash.

Raj P.: Also consider DAGs that read old messages (archive). We need the old KEK material to remain available for >= retention window + replay window. So rotation window must be coordinated with data retention policies.

Jess S.: For cross-cloud keys (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) we must keep a canonical version field in ciphertext metadata so service knows which provider/version to call. Example metadata change proposal:
```json
{"v":2, "provider":"aws","region":"us-west-2","key_id":"arn:aws:kms:..../key/abc","wrapped_dek":"...","alg":"RSA-OAEP-256"}
```
This lets us implement logic: if provider != current_preferred then we can rewrap later.

Anya (crypto): On backward compatibility: we should support v1 and v2 formats in readers for 6 months. Migration job should be optional — best-effort rewrap with canary sampling.

Mike (eng-ops): Implementation concerns: 1) RBAC — rotation will require adding service role privileges for rewrap (kms:ReEncrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt) across providers. Need least-privilege policies for rotate-worker. 2) Audit logging — every rewrap must generate an audit event (who, which key, old->new key mapping).

Lisa SRE: We also need a kill-switch for the rewrap job. If rewrap causes latency regressions, ops must be able to pause and resume. Suggest: track progress via a control table and expose a toggled feature flag.

Raj P.: About rollout timing: propose staged plan:
- Week 0: config + RBAC changes (no traffic).
- Week 1-2: run canary rewrap on small tenant set (1% of rows) with monitoring for latency, error-rate, KMS throttling.
- Week 3-4: increase to 10% then 50% if metrics OK.
- Week 6: full rollout.
Keep old KEKs for 90 days after full rollout.

Anya (crypto): For multi-provider strategy: we should avoid cross-provider rewraps unless requested. E.g., if a customer's key is in Azure Key Vault, don't migrate them to AWS KEK automatically. But we should ensure our code paths are generic so rewrap worker can call provider-specific API.

Jess S.: Tests: unit tests for metadata parsing, integration tests hitting each provider's encrypt/decrypt, and a local dry-run mode for rewrap job that counts operations without calling KMS.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rotation-worker:staging v0.3 -> started by @Mike (eng-ops)

Mike (eng-ops): For quotas we should implement client-side rate limiting and exponential backoff for KMS errors (LimitExceeded/Throttling). Also track consumed KMS requests in our metrics (per-provider).

Lisa SRE: Add alert when KMS 5xx or throttling > 1% baseline during rewrap. Also ensure SLO on read latency unaffected: if rewrap is slow, reads should fallback to old ciphertext path and not block.

Anya (crypto): Open question: do we rotate DEKs periodically too (short-lived DEKs) and keep KEKs long-lived? Suggest DEKs are rotated per-customer every 30 days, KEKs rotated per-provider every 90 days. Thoughts?

Jess S.: DEK rotation per-customer is heavy. Alternative: rotate DEK on vault-rotation event or on explicit customer request. Or rotate DEKs lazily when accessed after N days. Lazy rotation reduces churn.

Raj P.: Lazy rotation + background rewrap works well. For customers with compliance needs, offer an explicit "force rewrap" endpoint. That endpoint will require elevated RBAC and audit logging.

Anya (crypto): Action items:
- Jess: update metadata schema and draft migration compatibility table. (ETA 2d)
- Mike: plan rollback-safe rewrap worker with rate limiting + toggle + metrics. (ETA 1w)
- Lisa: run capacity test with fake rewrap load to validate SLOs. (ETA 1w)
- Raj: check retention + compliance windows and propose KEK hold duration. (ETA 3d)

Jess S.: Acked. I'll PR the schema changes and add sample migration scripts.

Lisa SRE: I'll schedule a chaos run for rewrap-worker in staging to ensure pause/resume works.

Mike (eng-ops): Will add RBAC Terraform changes for the rotate-role and a small runbook for incident response.

Anya (crypto): Great. If anyone wants to be added to the canary list DM me. I'll update the draft and ping again when PRs are ready. :sparkles:

Raj P.: +1 — thanks.

Jess S.: thanks all :thumbsup:
